subsystems.name: Hardware characterisation
subsystems.role: measures how badly each gate, qubit and readout actually behaves on a specific machine.

subsystems.name: Noise model
subsystems.role: a mathematical description of the errors the mitigation will try to undo.

subsystems.name: Circuit transformation layer
subsystems.role: rewrites the intended circuit into forms the hardware can then be run in to expose or cancel noise.

subsystems.name: Execution and scheduling
subsystems.role: runs hundreds to millions of circuit variants on real hardware and collects the shot statistics.

subsystems.name: Classical post-processing
subsystems.role: combines the noisy results into one corrected estimate.

buildSteps.title: Characterise the device
buildSteps.detail: Run standard benchmarking suites to obtain error rates per gate and per qubit, plus readout fidelities, on the exact machine that will be used.

buildSteps.title: Build a noise model
buildSteps.detail: Turn those measurements into channel descriptions — depolarising, amplitude damping, dephasing, crosstalk — for each operation in the circuit.

buildSteps.title: Choose a mitigation strategy
buildSteps.detail: Pick the method that fits the dominant error: extrapolation for smooth scaling behaviour, quasi-probability sampling when channel inverses are well known, symmetry checks when the ideal answer must obey a conservation law.

buildSteps.title: Transform the circuit
buildSteps.detail: Insert extra gate pairs to amplify noise to known scale factors, split the circuit into many statistically weighted variants, or wrap it in randomised compiling so coherent errors scramble into simpler stochastic ones.

buildSteps.title: Run the batches
buildSteps.detail: Submit every variant to the hardware, often thousands of shots each, and record raw bitstring counts.

buildSteps.title: Combine the results
buildSteps.detail: Average each noise level separately, then either fit and extrapolate to zero noise, or sum the quasi-probability variants with positive and negative weights.

buildSteps.title: Validate and bound the error
buildSteps.detail: Compare against classically simulable circuits of similar structure, and report an uncertainty range rather than a single number.

buildSteps.title: Feed back to the stack
buildSteps.detail: Use the measured residual error to refine the noise model, then repeat for the next problem — mitigation is an iterative calibration loop, not a one-off fix.

prerequisites.why: mitigation improves results only if the underlying gates are good enough that signals are not buried entirely in noise.

pathway.milestone: mitigation built into cloud quantum services and used in published chemistry, materials and optimisation experiments
pathway.unlocks: results that are meaningfully better than raw noisy hardware on small problems.

pathway.milestone: hybrid schemes that layer mitigation on top of a few logical qubits protected by early error correction
pathway.unlocks: larger circuits than mitigation alone can rescue.

pathway.milestone: mitigation used as a calibration and diagnostics layer inside fault-tolerant machines
pathway.unlocks: faster identification of which physical errors dominate and where to spend correction overhead.

pathway.milestone: full error correction dominates and mitigation shrinks to a benchmarking role
pathway.unlocks: reliable deep circuits where accuracy no longer depends on exponential sampling overhead.
